apparatus.basis: Editor's bracket [ϣⲟⲩⲱϩ]; verb of throwing/casting that fits 'cast forth from heaven' parallel to line 9 ⲁϩϣⲟⲩⲱϩ ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ.

Editor's bracket [ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ]; directional 'inward' continuing the gathering action from line 12.
Surviving ⲙ[ at start and ⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ 'hour' at end suggest temporal phrase ⲙ̄ⲡⲓⲛⲉⲩ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ 'at that very hour' — common formula in this corpus.

notes.decision: Translated as 'waters' — Lycopolitan plural variant of ⲙⲟⲩⲉⲩⲉ (already in glossary as 'waters'). The ⲗ is a regular Lycopolitan dialectal feature in this scribe's plural. Distinct from ⲙⲟⲩⲗⲉⲩⲉ 'counsels' (Greek βουλεύω) glossed elsewhere — context here (falls from heaven, drawn upward from earth, paired with fire and darkness as cosmic elements) is unambiguously hydrological.

Translated as 'shore' — Coptic ⲥⲁⲡⲧ̄/ⲥⲡⲟⲧⲟⲩ 'shore, bank, strand.' Confirmed by line 37 plural ⲛⲥⲃ̄ⲧⲉⲩⲉ 'shores' that closes the chapter with the same root, framing the cosmographic image of seas-within-shores.

Translated as 'sail' — Greek loanword πλέω 'to sail' or related verbal noun. Context (ships) is unambiguous. Standard Manichaean cosmography: the great encircling sea is where the cosmic ships (sun, moon) sail.

Translated 'a place of going' — ⲙⲁⲍⲉ as Lycopolitan reflex of ⲙⲟⲟϣⲉ 'walk, go,' yielding 'a place of walking/path' for the luminaries — i.e. the orbital track. Cf. accumulated ⲙⲁⲉⲉ ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'walk downward.'
Translated as 'powers' — Lycopolitan ⲛⲅⲁⲙ = ⲛϭⲟⲙ 'powers' (cf. accumulated ⲛⲟ̄ⲁⲙ). The 'three powers' of wind/water/fire are the three cosmic elements being drawn upward through the cosmic Atlas.
Translated 'the midst' — Coptic ⲙⲏⲧⲉ 'middle, midst.' Spatial reference to the central cosmic axis through which refined elements ascend from the Omophoros to the firmaments above.

The chapter heading is displayed in three lines with the chapter number ⲙⲁ̄ (=41) repeated as decorative flanking ornament around the title text. Read in linear sequence: 'Chapter 41. Concerning the tongue of the seas.' I render each line literally as transcribed.
Translated 'sign' — Coptic ϫⲱⲣⲙ̄ 'wink, nod, signal.' Standard idiom ϯ ⲟⲩϫⲱⲣⲙⲉ = 'give a sign/signal.'
Form unclear; possibly ⲁⲩϭⲛ 'they found' or causative-perfect of an action verb. Translated tentatively as a verbal continuation. Flagged for parallels.
Translated 'regions' — possibly Lycopolitan ⲧⲟϣ 'boundary, region, district' in plural with possessive. Context (upper place of all the X) supports a topographic-collective reading.

Translated 'raised them up' — from ⲧⲁϩⲟ 'set up, raise, establish' (Lycopolitan ⲍ for ϩ) with 3pl object suffix. Fits the sequence: scatter wind upon them → blow upon them → raise them up → wash them forth.

Translated 'washed forth' — Coptic ⲉⲓⲱⲉ 'wash' with directional ⲁⲃⲁⲗ. The wind washes/cleanses the elements from the earth into the waters. Preserves the purificatory register dominant in the chapter.

Translated 'the Error and the Answering' — both glossed in accumulated vocabulary. ⲡⲥⲁⲣⲙⲉ = the Error/wandering principle; ⲡⲟⲩⲱⲍⲙⲉ = the answering/responding. Together they form the cosmic dyad of negative speech-action — what the three places-of-deceit (water/darkness/fire) emit and what is then driven away.
